mutations.before: const assetName = displayName !== undefined && displayName !== value ? displayName : undefined;
mutations.after: const assetName = displayName !== undefined && displayName !== displayName ? displayName : undefined;
mutations.because: The description is only ever an addition, so the gate that decides to add it is the pair of half-negations: a name was resolved, and the ref does not already say it. Compare the name with itself and the second half can never hold, so `assetName` is always undefined and the mirror keeps announcing a bare 36-character uuid — the exact gap this description was written for. The test that renders an id ref WITH a display name and reads the ids off `aria-describedby`, resolving one to `Asset: hydra-logo.png`, finds none and fails on `texts`.
command: the hidden field is described by the asset's name when the value is an id

mutations.because: The attribute is a list, not a claim: the caller wired their own `aria-describedby` (an error id, a hint) and this field appends to it. Dropping the caller's value silently deletes whatever they described — the field stops reading as invalid — while the join still returns a non-empty string, so nothing about the result says it was overwritten. The test that passes `aria-describedby="hint-1"` beside a real `<span id="hint-1">` and asserts the attribute carries exactly `hint-1 <new id>` sees one id and fails on the length.
command: a caller's own description is kept beside the name
